_comment: Committed LLM-quality baselines (project-score-9 Phase 3). Update values only from a real measurement run; each entry records how it was produced.

retrievalEval.notes: Real chunk_transcript + SentenceTransformer embeddings + Qdrant query_points over an ephemeral collection. Zero LLM spend. Regression proof 2026-07-12: chunker broken to 120-char/0-overlap chunks -> recall@3 0.524, MRR 0.500, floor test FAILED as designed; reverted.
retrievalEval.rerun: cd services/summarizer && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/eval/test_retrieval_eval.py -s  (needs Qdrant reachable at QDRANT_HOST:QDRANT_PORT)

faithfulnessJudge.notes: Haiku fast-tier judge with claim-localized context selection. ~20 LLM calls, ~$0.02.

goldenEval.notes: Fresh v7 baseline after the 2026-08-11 consistency overhaul (playbooks + forbidden enforcement, adaptive vision tiers, degrade-never-drop). 14 live entries incl. 5 real admin-video anchors (3 TCG unboxings with forbiddenComponents). Zero forbidden hits; gaming anchors 0.962/0.962/1.000; weakest entries (learning-double-slit 0.579, review-airpods 0.617) are expectation drift on legacy entries, not regressions — re-curate their expectedTabs/requiredComponents. forbidden_ok scoring term (weight 0.15) and --stability probe added this round; stability is REPORTED not gated until trend data accumulates. Pre-fix red baseline on the gaming anchors was 0.890 with component coverage 0.50/0.67.
goldenEval.produce: 1) healthy stack, EVAL_USER_* + LANGFUSE_* exported  2) python3 scripts/run_eval.py --noise-runs 2 --output reports/ --publish-run golden-baseline-$(date +%Y%m%d)  (two fresh bypassCache passes; writes dev/golden-dataset/noise.json with per-metric baseline + noise + layoutStability)  3) copy baseline.quality into averageOverall + set measuredAt, set failUnder slightly below it (e.g. baseline - 0.05), and commit with noise.json. Later runs: python3 scripts/gate.py --report reports/eval-<ts>.json (primary metrics quality / faithfulness / duplicateRate within noise + per-video assertions).
